title: All branches in a conditional structure should not have exactly the same implementation
description: Having all branches of a conditional structure (such as if/elif/else) with exactly the same implementation is almost always a mistake. It usually means that the developer intended to implement different logic for each branch, but either copy-pasted code or forgot to update the implementation. This makes the code harder to understand and maintain, and can hide real bugs.
message: All branches in this conditional structure have exactly the same implementation.
impact: Code with identical branches is confusing, harder to maintain, and may hide bugs or incomplete implementations.
recommendation: Ensure that each branch of a conditional structure implements distinct logic, or refactor the code to remove unnecessary branches.

noncompliant.description: Both branches of the conditional execute the same code, which is likely not intended.

compliant.description: Each branch of the conditional executes different code, making the logic clear.

why_is_this_an_issue: Identical branches in conditionals are almost always a sign of a programming error or incomplete implementation, and reduce code clarity.
how_to_fix: Review the logic in each branch and ensure that each one performs the intended, distinct operation. Remove or refactor branches that are not needed.

security_mappings.CWE: CWE-398: Indicator of Poor Code Quality
